feedback.goal: Stack the HMR candidate loop on the runtime-generation attestation branch while preserving both generation contracts and their fail-closed eligibility rules.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Run records preserve runtime_generation while adding independent candidate_generation evidence without weakening either contract.
Both generation identities bind only at session creation, checkpoints are candidate-ineligible, and final eligibility requires one unchanged admitted HMR generation.
Runtime generation remains DAL-024 and ADR 0005, HMR becomes DAL-025 and ADR 0006, and all source-bound capsules validate.
Focused integration, real pinned HMR composition, and the complete repository verification gate pass on the rebased stack.

outcome.summary: The HMR candidate loop now stacks cleanly on runtime-generation attestation with combined session binding, final-only candidate eligibility, reconciled contracts, and passing focused and repository-wide verification.

what_worked: Keeping runtime and candidate generation as independent recorder inputs preserved PR 5 behavior while making their shared session boundary explicit.
A combined recorder test proved both persisted identities and their different checkpoint/final qualification rules in one run.
The existing pinned Loader and HMR composition probe passed after the rebase without modifying the external checkout.
what_failed: The initial rebase stopped on eight overlapping recorder, contract, evidence, and capsule files plus requirement and ADR numbering collisions.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: Sibling feature branches independently claimed the same requirement and ADR numbers and competing recorder constructor seams.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Reserve requirement and ADR identifiers before parallel feature work and add an explicit multi-source recorder integration test when either generation contract changes.

evidence.summary: The HMR feature was replayed directly on the runtime-generation attestation commit.
DAL-024 owns runtime generation and DAL-025 owns the bounded HMR candidate loop; ADRs 0005 and 0006 preserve the same separation.
The recorder binds both optional generation sources once at session creation and independently derives runtime stability and final-only candidate eligibility.
Six focused suites passed 50 tests with one opt-in composition case skipped; the combined runtime and candidate-generation recorder proof passed.
Three HMR-focused suites passed 33 tests including the real pinned Loader/HMR admission and rollback case.
All three reconciled local knowledge capsules validated against their canonical sources.
Typecheck, build, 34 test files with 214 passing tests and 7 opt-in skips, capsule validation, policy verification, core evaluation, and benchmark evaluation all passed without a hard stop.

uncertainty.statement: No shared-profile mount, production candidate application, authoritative DSH runtime-generation producer, or awaited final-disposal boundary was exercised.
uncertainty.resolution: Keep these as separately approved upstream or deployment proofs; do not infer them from the local stacked integration tests.

notes: The repository owner approved stacking and reconciling the feature branches.
